title: Invertibility of quasi-coherent modules is fppf local on algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $\{q_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be a small fppf covering of algebraic spaces [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus]: the maps are flat and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts and jointly surjective. Let $M$ be a quasi-coherent module on the small etale structure sheaf of $X$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], with tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. If every $q_i^*M$ is a line module, then $M$ is a line module. Here a line module is etale locally isomorphic to the structure sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space], and on schemes corresponds to an ordinary invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module]. No Noetherianity, separatedness, quasi-compactness or finite-generation hypothesis on $X$ or $M$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 060X, lemma-finite-locally-free-descends, rank-one case; spaces-topologies.tex Tag 0DFQ, lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc, for fppf covers. Rank is detected after a faithfully flat residue-field extension on scheme charts.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $u:U\to X$ and, for each $i$, a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $e_i:A_i\to X_i$. Put $B_i=U\times_X A_i$, with projections $p_i:B_i\to U$ and $d_i:B_i\to A_i$. These fibre products are schemes because both factors are schemes mapping to the algebraic space $X$. The family $\{q_i e_i:A_i\to X\}$ is fppf, by the etale-to-fppf comparison and composition, and its base change $\{p_i:B_i\to U\}$ is an fppf covering of schemes. It is therefore an fpqc covering of $U$. All families are small; no quasi-compact atlas or finite subcover of $X$ is chosen.

source.place: Tag 060X (lemma-finite-locally-free-descends), etale localization; spaces-topologies.tex Tags 03Y9 and 0DFQ; topologies.tex Tag 022C.

proof.text: Let $N=u^*M$. This is quasi-coherent by preservation of quasi-coherence under tensor pullback. Set $r_i=e_i d_i:B_i\to X_i$. Since $d_i$ is the base change of the etale map $u$, it is etale, and composition makes $r_i$ etale. The commutative fibre-product square and the canonical tensor-composition isomorphisms give $p_i^*N\simeq r_i^*q_i^*M$. Explicitly the composition comparison sends $a\otimes(b\otimes m)$ to $a f^\sharp(b)\otimes m$ on either composite. Etale pullback is restriction to the localized site. Consequently $r_i^*q_i^*M$ is a line module: restrict the etale local trivializations of the given line module $q_i^*M$ and their structure-sheaf identifications. Thus every $p_i^*N$ is a line module.

source.place: Tag 060X, reduction to schemes; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03GA (lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent); sites-modules.tex Tag 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules).

proof.text: Apply the scheme Zariski/small-etale equivalence to $N$, obtaining a quasi-coherent ordinary module $F$ on $U$ with $F_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq N$. Its pullback comparison for every scheme morphism gives $(p_i^*F)_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq p_i^*N$. The equivalence identifies ordinary invertible modules with small-etale line modules, so each ordinary $p_i^*F$ is invertible, hence finite locally free of rank one. Apply clause (2) of scheme fpqc descent to the covering $\{p_i\}$ from Step 1, with the specified rank $r=1$. It reflects finite local freeness of that rank, so $F$ is finite locally free of rank one, equivalently invertible. This reflection requires only that $F$ be quasi-coherent; finite generation or presentation is a conclusion, not an extra hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent), 03LC (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent-functorial), 05VG (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties); lemma-finite-locally-free-descends and fixed-rank fibre calculation.

proof.text: The same scheme equivalence makes $N\simeq F_{\mathrm{et}}$ a line module. Choose an etale covering $\{V_a\to U\}$ trivializing $N$. The composites $V_a\to U\to X$ form an etale covering, and restriction there identifies $M$ with the structure sheaf. This is exactly the definition of a line module on $X$. If $X$ is empty, the empty covering already gives this condition; empty members of a nonempty covering cause no restriction. Thus the argument includes empty index sets when allowed and imposes none of the excluded global finiteness or separation hypotheses.
